rules: PUBLIC grants are never auto-mapped; they are proposals for a named group.
Direct user grants map to a proposed group and stay flagged.
A source privilege that is unverifiable at the read-only access tier is a GAP, never an assumption.
Only rows with status APPROVED may appear in an executable script.
Production-catalog grants are a STOP E action and are absent from this map.

mappings.target_statement: GRANT USE SCHEMA ON SCHEMA ow_tp.silver TO `ow-tp-billing-readers`
mappings.rationale: Oracle INHERIT PRIVILEGES on the owning schema is not a data-read grant. The only defensible target analogue is a named reader group; PUBLIC (Unity Catalog `account users`) is never auto-mapped.
mappings.blocks: nothing before STOP E; required before any consumer reads ow_tp.silver

mappings.target_statement: ALTER SCHEMA ow_tp.bronze OWNER TO `2e90bc1d-e9a1-4703-8c48-ad28ebb1864d`; ALTER SCHEMA ow_tp.silver OWNER TO `2e90bc1d-e9a1-4703-8c48-ad28ebb1864d`; ALTER SCHEMA ow_tp.gold OWNER TO `2e90bc1d-e9a1-4703-8c48-ad28ebb1864d`
mappings.rationale: Schema ownership in the migration catalog is already held by the migration principal (factory-doctor analytical_target_grants ok). The durable owner after cutover is an application/service identity the engagement has not named.

mappings.target_statement: GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA ow_tp.silver TO `ow-tp-billing-readers`
mappings.rationale: The read-only reader role maps cleanly to a read group on the analytical track. The group does not exist yet; creating account groups is an account-admin action outside the migration principal.
